sentences.text:
The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The accused forged the property documents of Sy. No.34/6 measuring 2 acres situated at Channasandra Village and created the GPA as if executed by late B.G.
Vishveshwaraiah and sold the sites in the said property to the CW2 and other purchasers using the forged GPA as genuine documents and the accused sold the sites in the said property to the various purchasers by using the forged GPA documents and thereby cheated the purchasers and the complainant and other witnesses.
On the first information lodged by the CW1, FIR came to be registered and after completion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for the above said offences.
3. After taking cognizance, this court has complied Section 207 of Cr.P.C. by supplying charge sheet materials to the accused.
The Charge read over and explained to the accused and he has not pleaded guilty of alleged offences and claimed to be tried.

4. The Prosecution in order to prove the case, examined P.W.1 to 10 and got marked Ex.P1 to 6 and Ex.D1 is marked in the cross-examination of PW10.
5.
The Statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded.
The accused has denied all the incriminating materials found against him and he has not led any defence evidence.
6. I heard learned APP and learned counsel appearing for the accused.

7. The points that arose for my consideration are:
:: P O I N T S ::
Point No.1 : Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that the accused forged the property documents of Sy. No.34/6 measuring 2 acres situated at Channasandra Village and created the GPA as if executed by late B.G.
Vishveshwaraiah and sold the sites in the said property to the CW2 and other purchasers using the forged GPA as genuine documents and thereby committed offence punishable under section 471 of IPC?
Point No.2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on the said date, time and place, the accused sold the sites in the said property to the various purchasers by using the forged GPA documents and thereby cheated the purchasers and the complainant and other witnesses and thereby committed offence punishable under section 420 of IPC?
Point No.3. What order?

sentences.text: After going through the records and hearing the learned APP and learned counsel for the accused.

I answer the above points as under :
 Point No.1 & 2 : In the Negative  Point No.3 : As per final order, for  the following:
 REASONS 9.
Point No.1 & 2
: As the facts involved in these points are common, in order to avoid repetition of facts, they are taken together for consideration.

10. The prosecution in order to prove its case has examined the witnesses as PW1, complainant as PW2, the witnesses as PW3 to 8, investigating officer as PW9 and 10 respectively and got marked statement of PW1 at Ex.P1, complaint at Ex.P2, Certified copy of the sale deed at Ex.P3, certified copy of the judgment passed in O.S.No.6336/2012 at Ex.P3 (Ex.P4 sale deed and Ex.P3 judgment are different documents and by oversight the judgment is marked as Ex.P3 and therefore Ex.P3 sale deed and Ex.P3 judgment are different documents).
The certified copy of the judgment passed in O.S. No.536/2005 at Ex.P4 statement of PW7 at Ex.P5, FIR at Ex.P6.

The certified copy of the sale deed dated 01.07.1995 at Ex.D1 (which is marked in the cross-examination of P.W.10.
11.

The prosecution has examined the complainant as PW2 and in his evidence he has deposed that,
the sites are formed by agricultural Laboures Housing Society in Sy.No.34/6 of Channasandra village and thereafter society issued the GPA in favour of its secretary B.G. Vishwesharaiah and the said secretary sold the sites to the members of the society and the complainant vendor purchased the site in the year 1998 and in the year 2012 one T. Manjunath started digging foundation in site No.848 and other members of the society raised the objections and thereafter came to know

that,
the accused created false GPA and based on the created GPA created the false documents and sketch and executed the 20 sale deeds in the year 2011 in favour of 20 persons by mentioning the wrong site numbers and thereafter the witnesses approached the Kengeri police station and lodged the complaint and identified the complaint at Ex.P2 and identified the sale deed executed by the accused in favour of CW2 at Ex.P3 and produced certified copy of the judgments of O.S.No.6336/2012 and 536/2005 at Ex.P3 and 4 respectively.
The PW2 is cross-

examined and in the cross-examination he deposed that, he does not know how the society obtained the Sy.No.34/6 property and further stated that, the judgment produced by him at Ex.P3 and 4 in which the accused was not a party and further admitted that, neither the society nor the complainant filed the said suits and further clearly stated that, there is no mentioning of GPA dated 08.04.1997 in the Ex.P3 and 4 and therefore the evidence of PW2 does not prove that, the said Sy. No. Property is belonged to the society and it does not prove the alleged GPA created by the accused and further the said GPA is not at all produced before the court to prove the same and therefore the evidence of PW2 is not at all helpful to the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused.
12. The prosecution has examined the witnesses as PW3 to 6 and 8 and in their evidence they have deposed that, the Co-operative society executed the GPA in favour of the one Sridhar and the said Sridhar sold the site No.56A in favour of PW3, property No.849(A) in favour of PW6, further D Narasimhamurthy vs Thammanna on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130893679/

3 deposed that, the Co-operative society executed the GPA in favour of the Sridhar and the said Sridhar sold the site No.856 in favour of PW4 and one Jagadeesh, obtained the GPA from the Co-operative Society and sold the site no.855 in favour of PW5 and one Nagaraj was allotted site No.858 from the society and PW8 purchased the same from the said Nagaraj and contend that, the accused created GPA as if executed by Visveshwariah and based on the created GPA sold the sites in Sy.No.34/6 to various persons by showing wrong site numbers and thereby cheated the society and their members by creating the forged GPA.

The PW4 to 6 and 8 have not at all produced any documents before the court to show that, Sy. No.34/6 property is belonged to the Co-operative Society and they have not even placed the GPA before this court to prove the alleged forgery committed by the accused and further in the cross- examination they have deposed that, they do not know how the society obtained Sy.No.34/6 property and they have not placed any materials before the court to show Sy.No.34/6 property is belonged to the Society.

13. Further the PW5 witness in the cross- examination admitted that, on 08.04.1997 Late Vishweshwaraiah executed the GPA in favour of the accused Thammanna and further PW6 in the cross- examination deposed that, Late Vishweshwaraiah has not sold Sy.No.34/6 property in favour of the society and therefore the evidence of PW3 to 6 and PW8 does not prove that, Sy.No.34/6 is belonged to the Co-operative Society and their evidence does not prove the alleged forgery committed by the accused and therefore the evidence of PW3 to 6 and 8 is not helpful to the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

14. The prosecution has examined the witnesses as PW1 and 7 and in their evidence they have deposed that, they do not know about the case and they have not given any statement to the police and they were treated as hostile witnesses and they were cross-examined by the learned App by suggesting that, the accused forged the GPA as if executed by late Vishveshwaraiah and based on the forged documents sold the sites in Sy.No.34/6 and thereby cheated the members of the society.
But all these suggestions were denied by the PW1 and 7 and nothing worthy was elicited in the course of the cross-examination in favour of the prosecution.

15. Further the investigating officer is examined as PW9 and he deposed that, based on the complaint lodged by the CW1 he registered FIR as per Ex.P6 and recorded the statement of witnesses and got released the accused on bail bonds as per the anticipatory bail order and submitted the further investigation to PW10.

The prosecution has examined the investigating officer as PW10 and he deposed that, after recording the statement of CW2 and 3 and after completion of investigation filed the charge sheet against the accused.

PW10 is cross- examined and in the cross-examination he has admitted that, Sy.No.34/6 measuring 02 acres is the property belong to one B.G. Vishweshwaraiah and further admitted that, he has not at all obtained the documents containing the signatures of the B. G. Vishweshwaraiah and he has not even seized original GPA and he has not sent any GPA for FSL analysis and he has not at all obtained any property documents pertaining to Sy.No.34/6 and further admitted that, he has not obtained any documents to show that, Sy.No.34/6 property is belonged to Co- operative Society and further admitted that, he has not at all examined the family members of the B.G. Vishweshwaraiah and further clearly stated that,
neither the family members of B.G. Vishweshwaraiah nor the Co-operative Society given any complaint against the accused and therefore the investigating officer has utterly failed to place any D Narasimhamurthy vs Thammanna on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130893679/
4 records before the court to show that, Sy.No.34/6 property is belonged to the Co-operative Society and investigating officer has not placed any records before the court to show that, the accused has created the GPA.
In this case the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the alleged guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence accused is entitled for the benefit of doubt.

entities.text: Bhagwan Jaganath Markand v/s State of Maharashtra reported in 2016 (1) SCC 537
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have carefully perused the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and also the materials on record, the evidence produced by prosecution has failed to carry a high degree of probability with regard to the alleged offences committed by the accused.
Therefore, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt and accused is entitled to be Acquitted.
Hence, with the above observations, I hold point No.1 & 2 in the NEGATIVE.
17. Point No.3:

For the reasons stated and discussion made above, I proceed to pass the following ;
ORDER
The accused is ACQUITTED U/s 248(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable U/s 471 and 420 of I.P.C.
The bail bonds executed by accused shall be continued for a period of six months.
